Turkey Tracing Worksheets For Preschoolers And Up

Thanksgiving is a great time to sneak a little handwriting practice into your day, especially when there are silly turkeys involved! These turkey tracing worksheets give preschool and kindergarten kids a chance to work on their pencil control with letter tracing, different types of lines, and a turkey picture they can finish themselves.

If your kids could use some extra practice before they start writing letters and words on their own, check out our other free printable tracing worksheets for kids. You’ll find more simple activities to help them get comfortable holding and using a pencil.

Fun Turkey Printables

I think the turkeys make these pages a little more interesting than the usual tracing worksheets. One turkey is holding an umbrella, while the others are waiting for kids to trace the paths between them. There’s enough variety that they won’t feel like they’re doing the same thing over and over.

As kids follow the dotted lines, they’re practicing the small hand movements they’ll need for writing. They’ll also work on hand-eye coordination, pencil control, and recognizing uppercase and lowercase letters.

These pages are easy to print for a Thanksgiving activity at home or in the classroom. You can use them for morning work, a writing center, or a little extra fine motor practice without having to prepare anything else.

Trace The Turkey

This poor turkey looks like he’s trying to stay dry under his umbrella! Kids will trace the dashed lines to finish his feathers and other details, then color him however they’d like. It’s a nice change from tracing plain lines, and they get a complete picture to show off when they’re finished.

Tt Letter Tracing Practice

Since turkey starts with T, it’s a good excuse to practice writing that letter. This worksheet has kids tracing uppercase and lowercase T’s on handwriting lines, with a little turkey at the top to remind them what they’re working on. They can start by following the dotted letters and work toward writing them with less help.

Trace The Lines Between The Turkeys

Those turkeys at the bottom are waiting for their friends to make it down the page! Kids will trace different paths from one turkey to another, including stair-step lines, curves, and zigzags. Some are easier to follow than others, so it’s good practice for slowing down and keeping their pencil on the line.

Turkey Trouble – If you’ve never read this book, you have to add it to your holiday collection! It’s so cute and fun and kids just love it! Follow the turkey around the farm as he disguises himself as different animals so the farmer doesn’t catch him for Thanksgiving dinner!

How To Catch A Turkey – Kids who love the How To Catch books will want to see all the crazy contraptions kids make to try to catch a turkey loose at the school!

Pete The Cat: The First Thanksgiving -Every Pete the Cat book is fantastic, but this one takes it up a notch with flaps for the kids to open. It’s a great way to get the kids excited about reading and Thanksgiving!

Fall Holiday Crafts Kids Will Love

Turkey Shape Craft: Who knew you could make a turkey from a bunch of basic shapes? Kids use circles, triangles, and rectangles to put together their own colorful bird, complete with a big fan of feathers. I like that you can talk about the shapes as they put everything together, so they get some extra learning in without making it feel like a lesson.

Mayflower Handprint Craft: This is a cute way to turn your child’s handprint into something other than the usual turkey. Their hand becomes one of the Mayflower’s sails, and the rest of the ship is made with simple paper pieces. It’s also a nice opportunity to talk about the Mayflower and the journey across the ocean. Plus, you’ll have a little keepsake showing just how small their hand was that year.

Turkey Headband Craft: Can you imagine a classroom full of kids wearing these colorful turkey headbands? The big feathers sticking up behind their heads would make such a cute picture. Kids can make theirs with construction paper or use the black-and-white version and color it themselves. Either way, they’ll have something to wear for Thanksgiving festivities.

Pumpkin Pie Craft: I think the little dollop of whipped cream on top is what really makes this paper pumpkin pie cute. Kids put together their own slice, add a happy face, and place it on a paper plate like it’s ready to serve. It’s especially fitting if you’re doing Thanksgiving crafts while the real pies are baking. And unlike the real thing, this slice can go home in a backpack!

Autumn Learning Pages

Have you read How to Catch a Turkey with your kids yet? The turkey running loose around the school makes it such a funny Thanksgiving story. These How to Catch a Turkey activities keep the theme going with pilgrim patterns, a letter P dot marker page, tracing lines, and more. The pattern activity is especially nice because kids get to cut and paste the missing pictures instead of just circling an answer.

There’s always room for a little extra learning before Thanksgiving break, especially when you can use pictures of pumpkins and turkeys instead of plain worksheets. These Thanksgiving worksheets have kids finishing holiday patterns, finding their way through a letter C maze, and practicing the letter T. I like the mix because you can work on a few different skills without printing a huge packet.

Dabbing markers are one of those supplies that make kids feel like they’re playing instead of doing schoolwork. With these turkey do a dot printables, they can fill in a turkey, find uppercase and lowercase T’s, and practice counting with dots. You could also use small stickers on the circles if you don’t want to get the markers out.

It’s always fun to see kids figure out what a dot to dot picture is going to be before they’ve connected all the numbers. These turkey connect the dots give them three different pictures to finish, including a turkey dinner on a platter. They’ll practice counting up to 20 on one page, while another mixes numbers and letters. Once the pictures are complete, kids can color them in for a little extra Thanksgiving fun.
